description: Added a 'Classifying carefully — do not over-classify' section instructing that a single refusal/action is one behavior and not to add a spurious second behavior (e.g. an extra 'safety') from the same action. Addresses the recurring pattern of extra safety/escape behaviors appearing alongside avoidance.

Clarified that a child merely stating or explaining their fear is not reassurance-seeking; only label 'safety'/reassurance when the note shows the child actually sought comfort or protection. Addresses inferred reassurance framing.
Added rule to not attach interpretive parentheticals or inferred functions (e.g. 'coercive behavior to get parent to stay') unless the note states that function.
Added rule that a parent/adult action (allowed, let, arranged) is an accommodation and must not be converted into a separately reported child behavior.

Added guidance to use 'unclear' once for an ambiguous note rather than repeatedly, and to pick the single best-fitting type when an action could fit two. Addresses duplicate-unclear and double-count failures.
Strengthened the Situations instruction to not drop a distinct trigger because it seems minor or the response is brief. Addresses missed situations.
Qualified the existing 'Reassurance-seeking is safety' rule and the split rule with conservative caveats (only when actually sought; do not split a single action).
